content.definition: Business arrangement where two or more parties agree to pool resources for specific purpose or project. Each party has joint control.
content.accounting_method: Typically EQUITY METHOD (ASC 323) because no single party has control (even if 50% ownership)

equity_method_application.initial_investment: DR Investment in Joint Venture, CR Cash
equity_method_application.share_of_income: DR Investment in JV, CR Equity in JV Income
equity_method_application.share_of_loss: DR Equity in JV Loss, CR Investment in JV
equity_method_application.distributions_received: DR Cash, CR Investment in JV
equity_method_application.basis_difference: Amortize if cost exceeds book value of net assets acquired

consolidation_exception.when_consolidate: If one party has control (>50% voting control AND power to direct activities), consolidate instead of equity method
consolidation_exception.typical_jv: Usually 50/50 or similar split → No single control → Equity method

proportionate_consolidation.not_gaap: Proportionate consolidation (reporting proportionate share of JV's assets, liabilities, revenues, expenses) NOT permitted under US GAAP
proportionate_consolidation.ifrs_note: IFRS permits proportionate consolidation for some joint arrangements, but US GAAP does not

nonmonetary_assets.general_rule: Recognize gain/loss on contribution based on fair value
nonmonetary_assets.exception: If contribution lacks commercial substance or FV not reliably measurable, may defer gain

example.facts: Company A and Company B form 50/50 joint venture. Each contributes $500K cash. JV has net income $200K Year 1, pays $50K distributions.
company_a_entries: Investment: DR Investment in JV $500K, CR Cash $500K
Income: DR Investment in JV $100K (50% × $200K), CR Equity in JV Income $100K
Distribution: DR Cash $25K (50% × $50K), CR Investment in JV $25K

intercompany_transactions.upstream_sales: JV sells to venturer. Defer venturer's share of profit until realized.
intercompany_transactions.downstream_sales: Venturer sells to JV. Defer profit on sale until JV sells to third party or consumes asset.
intercompany_transactions.full_deferral: Defer 100% of profit on downstream sales (venturer controls transaction)

financial_statement_presentation.balance_sheet: Investment in Joint Venture (single line under equity method)
financial_statement_presentation.income_statement: Equity in Joint Venture Income (single line)
financial_statement_presentation.cash_flow_statement: Distributions received: Operating activities (if from JV operations)

disclosures: Nature and extent of interest in joint ventures
Summarized financial information of JV (if material)
Restrictions on ability to distribute earnings

vs_partnership.joint_venture: Specific purpose, limited duration. Typically separate legal entity. Venturers use equity method.
vs_partnership.partnership: Ongoing business. Partners are partnership itself (not separate investors). Partners use partnership accounting (capital accounts, income allocation per agreement).

variable_interest_entity_consideration.if_jv_is_vie: Evaluate if venturer is primary beneficiary. If yes, consolidate. If no, equity method.
variable_interest_entity_consideration.indicators: Thinly capitalized JV, venturer guarantees JV's debt, venturer has controlling financial interest

cpa_exam_tips: Joint venture: Typically equity method (no single party has control)
Proportionate consolidation NOT allowed under US GAAP
Investment increases by share of income, decreases by distributions
Defer intercompany profit (downstream: 100%, upstream: investor's share)
One-line consolidation: Investment in JV (BS), Equity in JV Income (IS)

key_points: Joint venture: Two or more parties with joint control, no single party controls
Accounting: Equity method (not consolidation unless one party has control)
Proportionate consolidation NOT permitted under US GAAP
Defer intercompany profits (100% downstream, investor's share upstream)
One-line consolidation presentation in financial statements
